unit.why: Inside a homiletic discussion on the burdens of the rabbinate, the division tells an anecdote about the Hatam Sofer, a non-Hasidic rabbinic authority. He flees a match offered with the promise of a rabbinate, and his teacher, the Mahatsit ha-Shekel, foretells that he will become a rabbi against his will.
unit.boundary_note: the division begins mid-quotation from a book; it ends with the heading 'מענין רצון', which belongs to the next division

stories.start_quote: ושמעתי אומר בשם רבינו הח״ס ז״ל
stories.summary_en: The young Hatam Sofer leaves a wealthy match because the prospective father-in-law promised to obtain a rabbinate for him. His teacher, the Mahatsit ha-Shekel, foretells that he will become a rabbi against his will, which comes true; the Hatam Sofer later told the story to his students with a sigh and endured great poverty before taking a post.
